decisions.executionNote: Begin separate elbow-up approaches toward red and yellow nuts, raising wrists while turning grippers downward; refine from wrist views.
Finish downward orientation and descend above the visually localized red and yellow nuts, keeping each arm on its own side.
Use wrist-image offsets to center both nuts, close grippers, and lift briefly to check visual retention.
Both nuts appear retained. Transport toward separated central staging locations for exchange, with wrists raised and grippers closed.
Replan after continuity rejection: smaller motions downward and backward to ease elbow flexion, staging nuts at two separated centerline locations.
Set both nuts down on the centerline, release, and withdraw outward and upward before exchanging pickup locations.
Exchange approach lanes while separated, then approach the staged yellow nut with the left arm and red nut with the right.
Center on staged nuts, descend to grasp height, close and withdraw toward each matching bolt; verify retention visually.
Red nut appears retained; carry it above the red bolt. Yellow was not retained, so reopen, recenter on its shifted position and retry the grasp.
Retry yellow at its newly shifted tabletop center. Lower retained red nut onto the red stud and begin a slow clockwise engagement.
Allow a longer stationary closure around yellow before lifting. Continue the red nut's first clockwise tightening stroke with small axial descent.
Correct rejected tensor; no prior motion occurred. Recenter and close on yellow, finish the red stroke, release, and begin wrist reset.
Red nut visibly separated on release, so regrasp at its new location. Lift yellow to test retention and transport toward the yellow stud.
Yellow remained on table; approach its latest center at a lower grasp height. Lift regrasped red nut and align above the red stud using current head geometry.
Use wrist-plane image offsets for yellow's grasp correction. Lower red onto its stud with a small lateral adjustment and gentle clockwise engagement.
Yellow appears below the fingertips: retry a lower grasp. Lift the red nut clear to inspect its axial alignment rather than continuing a tilted insertion.
Correct yellow pickup using the measured wrist-image motion direction, then test a lift. Lower red vertically without additional twisting to inspect seating.
Yellow is now visibly retained; carry it above its matching stud. Release the skewed red nut gently at the stud and withdraw to inspect whether it settles upright.
Visually center yellow over its stud and descend without twisting. Red settled beside its stud; regrasp lower on the nut for a straighter insertion.
Yellow stud is visible inside the hole; make a small centering adjustment, seat and turn clockwise. Lift red clear and recenter above its stud.
Continue yellow clockwise, release for a wrist reset. Align and lower red slowly onto its stud while watching seating.
Yellow remains upright with its stud visible near the top; withdraw and approach purple. Correct red's fore-aft alignment after lifting slightly, then test engagement.
Pick purple at a lower centered grasp and test retention. Complete a short red tightening stroke and release to inspect whether it seats upright.
Stage retained purple on the centerline for the right arm. Red did not remain engaged; reset the right wrist above its new tabletop position for a straighter regrasp.
Release purple at the staging point and return left toward yellow for additional tightening. Lower the reset right gripper straight onto red and close.
Yellow looks upright with the stud near flush; leave it released and withdraw left. Recenter the right grasp on red using its wrist-image offset and test retention.
Red appears retained in the lower grasp. Lift well clear of the stud before translating above it, then inspect alignment before descent.
Lower the centered red nut gradually and test a small clockwise engagement. Begin a slow continuous left-arm return toward its origin.
Continue the red clockwise tightening stroke with a small axial descent while completing the left arm's continuous return to origin.
Release red without translation and reset the wrist for another tightening stroke; check that the nut remains aligned rather than falling aside.
Red remained upright and aligned after release. Regrasp slightly lower and perform another clockwise tightening stroke with minimal axial feed.
Release red in place and reset the wrist while open for another tightening stroke, preserving the seated alignment.
Regrasp the seated red nut slightly lower and tighten another clockwise stroke, feeding down only minimally.
Release and leave the aligned red pair, reset and lift clear, then approach the staged purple nut with the right arm.
Descend over the central purple nut with the right gripper, adjust wrist angle while open, and close stationary for pickup.
Purple remained below the fingers. Reopen, correct toward its wrist-image location, and grasp lower before testing a lift.
Purple is off-center and tilted against a jaw. Reopen and shift across the wrist image before regrasping without pressing farther into the table.
Purple is centered between the jaws. Lift clear, make a small downward-axis correction, and carry above its matching stud.
Center purple over its visible stud, lower vertically in small increments, and begin a gentle clockwise engagement.
Make a millimeter-scale purple centering correction and continue clockwise with minimal axial feed while keeping the nut upright.
Finish the purple clockwise stroke, release without translation, and reset the wrist while open to check that engagement persists.
Purple remained upright after release. Regrasp slightly lower and apply another controlled clockwise tightening stroke.
Release purple in place and reset the open wrist for another tightening stroke, keeping the axis stationary.
Regrasp purple slightly lower and tighten clockwise again with a small axial feed, keeping the other arm at rest.
Release the tightened purple nut, lift clear without pulling it, and begin withdrawing the right arm toward origin.
Return both open grippers to their original poses along continuous elbow-up paths, leaving the three assembled color pairs undisturbed.
Settle both open grippers precisely at origin and observe whether the assembled pairs remain stable.
The episode remains active and red still shows thread depth; return above red for additional tightening without disturbing yellow or purple.
Regrasp red at its lowered seated height with a vertical wrist, then begin an additional clockwise tightening stroke.
Continue red clockwise with a small axial feed, then release in place to inspect the remaining depth.
Reset the open right wrist and regrasp red in place for another short tightening pass.
Advance the red nut another controlled clockwise stroke, with a small downward feed to follow the thread.
Release and reset without moving the red nut laterally, then reclose for further thread advancement.
Allow closure to settle, then continue red clockwise while following the thread downward by a small amount.
Release red and reset the open wrist while preserving its axis; the stud remains recessed, so prepare another short tightening pass.
Regrasp and make one further controlled clockwise pass on red with a small downward thread-following feed.
Release red after the added tightening passes, lift clear, and withdraw toward origin with both grippers open.
Return the open right gripper to origin along a continuous elbow-up path; leave the stable assembled pairs untouched.
Settle both open grippers at their original poses and check the stable assembled pairs.
Hold both arms at origin with grippers open while observing the three stable, color-matched assembled pairs.
Maintain both open grippers at origin, correcting only small tracking drift and leaving the assembled pairs undisturbed.
Purple still appeared slightly recessed on the last close view; approach it for an additional controlled tightening pass while leaving yellow and red untouched.
Center over the seated purple nut, regrasp at its lowered height, and add a short clockwise tightening stroke.
Continue purple's clockwise tightening with a small thread-following descent, then release and begin an open-wrist reset.
Finish the open-wrist reset and regrasp the upright purple nut without changing its lateral alignment.
Advance purple through another clockwise stroke with a gentle axial feed, watching for the stud to approach the nut's upper face.
Release purple in place and reset the open wrist for another tightening stroke, maintaining the same axis.
Regrasp purple and apply another clockwise tightening pass, following the thread down by only a few millimeters.
Release purple after the added tightening, lift clear, and withdraw toward origin with the gripper fully open.
Return both open grippers to their original poses without disturbing the three aligned assemblies.
Settle both open grippers precisely at their original poses, with the three color-matched assemblies left stable on the table.
Approach yellow with the left arm for a final tightening check; keep the right gripper open at origin and preserve elbow-up continuity.
Center and regrasp the seated yellow nut with a vertical wrist, then add a small clockwise tightening pass.
Complete yellow's clockwise pass with a small downward feed, then release and reset while keeping the nut axis fixed.
Reset the open left wrist and regrasp yellow for one more controlled tightening stroke without further downward pressing.
Apply another clockwise yellow tightening stroke without axial pressing, then release in place.
Yellow appears seated near flush. Lift the open left gripper clear and withdraw toward origin without disturbing the three assemblies.
